10	# WI-027: Demo Constraint Execution (STELLARATOR-DEMO Item 2)
11	
12	**Required Reading: `knowledge/holdout/aries-cs/PROTOCOL.md`** — this is a stellarator-demo model-development item. The ARIES-CS hold-out is sealed; the §3 barred paths must not be read, cited, or opened. No barred artifact was read at this spec. Admissible sources touched here: the canonical viability model (`models/library/analyses/mfe_viability.sysml`, the two `models/designs/` plant instances), the staged demo package under `exploration/stellarator_e2e/`, and the in-repo IFE constraint-exec acceptance in the primary checkout (`~/1cfe/fusion-tea/exploration/ife_e2e/study/`). All admissible.
13	
14	**Orchestration brief: `work/orchestration/demo-constraint-execution.md`** — Align rulings, graded inputs, standing bars. This spec executes that brief; everything there is load-bearing and is not re-derived or contradicted here. **Governing frame: `.project/concepts/stellarator-mbse-demo.md`, criterion 2** — done-ness runs against that criterion, not against any adjacent epic's items. Tracking home: `.project/backlog/epic_stellarator_mbse_demo.md`, Item 2.
15	
16	**Pipeline note (Align ruling 1, [OWNER] 2026-07-19):** the post-spec owner checkpoint is **waived** for this item — the pipeline runs spec → design without an owner pause. This spec is therefore written to be complete enough that design needs no scope clarification. Where a decision is genuinely mechanism (how the model is built), it is named and handed to design explicitly, not left implicit.
17	
18	## Overview
19	
20	Criterion 2 of the stellarator demo requires that viability checks execute *as modeled constraints* — the physics/economics limits are `assert constraint`s in the canonical SysML model, they run through the generated pipeline, and their verdicts (`satisfied | violated | indeterminate`) appear as data in the run report — **with no hand-coded viability rule anywhere in the demo pipeline**. The model already carries the five constraints; the generated demo pipeline does not execute them.
21	
22	Two things block the criterion today:
23	
24	1. The staged demo copies under `exploration/stellarator_e2e/` **strip the asserts before codegen**. When the stellarator model was first run end-to-end (2026-07-13), the newer codegen strict mode (INV-2) resolved `assert constraint` actuals and aborted on plain design-attribute actuals; constraint execution was Stage-4 scope, so the staged copies commented the five assert blocks out (CODEGEN_FINDINGS #9). The strip comments sit at the staged `mfe_plant.sysml:459-465` and the staged `stellarator_plant.sysml:741-746`.
25	2. The constraint-execution toolchain that fills that seam is now **delivered and proven in-repo** — the IFE acceptance (`~/1cfe/fusion-tea/exploration/ife_e2e/study/`, 2294/2301, 2026-07-13) ran the retiring hand rule and the now-executing generated `'Viability Threshold'` predicate together over the full 2301-point grid; the 7-row divergence is the documented `>` vs `>=` boundary hazard, not a defect. The generated package emits constraint-predicate modules and a `ConstraintReportAggregatorModule`, and verdicts flow to the run report as data.
26	
27	This item regenerates the staged stellarator package with constraint lowering: the five asserts flow through codegen instead of being stripped, verdicts appear in the run report at the Stellaris design point, and the hand-off retires the strip. This is a **refinement-type item** — it adds constraint *verdicts* as additive data; every already-computed numeric value stays bit-exact, and the handshake must not move.
28	
29	**Baseline (executed record carried in — WI-025, `work/completed/20260718_WI-025_stale-basis-pass-through-recompute/`):** total $12,638,857,665.74, LCOE $203.647152/MWh, p_net 915.081088 MW, q_eng 6.606662, rec_frac 0.151362, magnet $6,323,469,946.33 (50.03%); every executed channel bit-exact vs oracle at rel 1e-9. This item does not move any of these numbers — it adds five verdicts alongside them.
30	
31	## Goals & Context
32	
33	**Demo criterion served (governing bar, verbatim — `.project/concepts/stellarator-mbse-demo.md` criterion 2):**
34	> **Viability checks execute as modeled constraints** — Physics viability limits (candidates: confinement-scaling consistency, beta/density limits, wall load, TBR floor) are modeled as `assert constraint`s and execute via the constraint-execution machinery, with verdicts (satisfied / violated / indeterminate) appearing as data in run reports — no hand-coded viability rules anywhere in the demo.
35	
36	**Research questions served (OVERVIEW.md):** RQ (viability/feasibility). Constraint verdicts turn "is this design point viable?" from a prose claim or harness `if` into modeled, executed, reported data — the one-notch-deeper capability the concept calls out (initial model includes viability physics as assert constraints, "one notch deeper than 1costingFE's fixed-operating-point power balance").
37	
38	**Decision-carrying inputs, graded (from the orchestration brief; carry the grades, do not reopen):**
39	
40	- **[OWNER] (epic Item 2, ratified frame):** verdicts appear as data in the demo run report at the Stellaris design point; **no hand-coded viability rule anywhere in the demo pipeline**.
41	- **[OWNER] 2026-07-19, Align ruling 3:** the executing-constraint set = **everything already modeled, nothing new**. The canonical asserts (`net_positive`, `recirc_ok` in `mfe_plant.sysml`; `beta_ok` / `wall_load_ok` / `tbr_ok` in the concept-09 instance) execute; ISS04 confinement-consistency and other candidates stay Stage-3 refinement material (concept Open Question 3 resolved for this item).
42	- **[OWNER 2026-07-19] (anchor spec ratification):** Item 2 is a **refinement-type** item under the amended successor bar — the **original bar applies unamended**: `handshake_1costingfe.py` editable only within `set_1cfe_inputs`'s injection map (no comparison-logic change), and `git diff exploration/stellarator_e2e/handshake_comparison.json` **must be empty**. Constraint verdicts are additive data; every computed value stays bit-exact.
43	- **[OWNER] 2026-07-19, Align ruling 1:** post-spec checkpoint waived (spec → design, no owner pause).
44	- **[OWNER] 2026-07-19, Align ruling 2:** owner holds close — audit runs, owner closes WI-027, orchestrator commits after close.
45	- **[OWNER-VERBATIM] (standing, WI-024 checkpoint):** "spec should capture the outcomes — how the model is built should be done with the expertise of SysML modeling." Mechanism is design's: how constraint lowering is invoked, how verdicts land in the report, exactly which staged edits retire, and the codegen local-state needed for constraint emission are all deferred to `/design-model`.
46	- **[AGENT] (orchestrator), orientation not owner intent:** the mechanism is regeneration of the staged stellarator package with constraint lowering, retiring the strip comment at the staged `stellarator_plant.sysml:741`. Design verifies mechanism details.
47	- **[INHERITED: `work/orchestration/stale-basis-recompute.md` §inherited]** — the standing validation bars (enumerated in Success Criteria below), re-verified at WI-025.
48	- **[INHERITED: PROTOCOL]** — §3 barred paths absolute; PROTOCOL listed as Required Reading.

**Required Reading: `knowledge/holdout/aries-cs/PROTOCOL.md`** — this is a stellarator-demo model-development item. The ARIES-CS hold-out is sealed; the §3 barred paths must not be read, cited, or opened. No barred artifact was read at this spec. ## Overview

Criterion 2 of the stellarator demo requires that viability checks execute *as modeled constraints* — the physics/economics limits are `assert constraint`s in the canonical SysML model, they run through the generated pipeline, and their verdicts (`satisfied | violated | indeterminate`) appear as data in the run report — **with no hand-coded viability rule anywhere in the demo pipeline**. The model already carries the five constraints; the generated demo pipeline does not execute them.

Two things block the criterion today:

1. The staged demo copies under `exploration/stellarator_e2e/` **strip the asserts before codegen**. When the stellarator model was first run end-to-end (2026-07-13), the newer codegen strict mode (INV-2) resolved `assert constraint` actuals and aborted on plain design-attribute actuals; constraint execution was Stage-4 scope, so the staged copies commented the five assert blocks out (CODEGEN_FINDINGS #9). The strip comments sit at the staged `mfe_plant.sysml:459-465` and the staged `stellarator_plant.sysml:741-746`.
2. The constraint-execution toolchain that fills that seam is now **delivered and proven in-repo** — the IFE acceptance (`~/1cfe/fusion-tea/exploration/ife_e2e/study/`, 2294/2301, 2026-07-13) ran the retiring hand rule and the now-executing generated `'Viability Threshold'` predicate together over the full 2301-point grid; the 7-row divergence is the documented `>` vs `>=` boundary hazard, not a defect. The generated package emits constraint-predicate modules and a `ConstraintReportAggregatorModule`, and verdicts flow to the run report as data.

This item regenerates the staged stellarator package with constraint lowering: the five asserts flow through codegen instead of being stripped, verdicts appear in the run report at the Stellaris design point, and the hand-off retires the strip. This is a **refinement-type item** — it adds constraint *verdicts* as additive data; every already-computed numeric value stays bit-exact, and the handshake must not move.

**Baseline (executed record carried in — WI-025, `work/completed/20260718_WI-025_stale-basis-pass-through-recompute/`):** total $12,638,857,665.74, LCOE $203.647152/MWh, p_net 915.081088 MW, q_eng 6.606662, rec_frac 0.151362, magnet $6,323,469,946.33 (50.03%); every executed channel bit-exact vs oracle at rel 1e-9. This item does not move any of these numbers — it adds five verdicts alongside them.

1	# S-FUSION (Appendix C): IFE acceptance + prepare-once benchmark
2	
3	CONSTRAINT-EXEC Item 14, W4. Repo: fusion-tea. Session: 2026-07-13.
4	
5	## Result
6	
7	**Acceptance: 100% agreement, modulo 7 flagged boundary rows.** The retiring hand rule
8	(`sweep_ife.py:82`, `eta * gain > 10`, strict `>`) and the now-executing generated
9	`'Viability Threshold'` constraint assertion (`eta * gain >= threshold`, `>=`) were replayed
10	once, together, over the full 2301-point `(eta, gain)` grid (`ETA_GRID` × `G_GRID`, matching
11	`sweep_ife.py`'s own grid exactly). 2294 rows match exactly; 7 rows sit exactly on
12	`eta*gain == 10.0` and diverge — this is the documented `>` vs `>=` boundary hazard
13	(`.project/reference/fusion-tea-ife-sweep/FACTS.md`), not a defect. See
14	`acceptance_table.csv` (columns: `eta, gain, eta_g, old_viable, new_verdict, new_viable,
15	at_boundary, match`).
16	
17	The hand rule at `sweep_ife.py:82` is retired: `sweep_ife.py`'s hot grid loop now calls the
18	generated predicate function (`ife_tea.modules.constraints.predicates
19	.constraint_pred_ife_plant__ife_power_plant__viability`) directly, the same mechanical-import
20	pattern the file already used for LCOE/recirculating-fraction. The LCOE-threshold overlay at
21	`:84` (`attractive = viable and power_positive and lcoe <= 100`) is untouched — policy, not a
22	modeled constraint, per FACTS.md.
23	
24	**Prepare-once benchmark** (`prepare_once_benchmark.json`, N=200 real evaluations against the
25	sealed package): prepare-once **~168x** faster than rebuild-per-case (0.166 ms/case prepared
26	vs 27.8 ms/case rebuilt), 200/200 verdict parity between the two paths. A recorded
27	measurement (S5 carry-forward (2)), not a tuning target.
28	
29	## Regenerated package
30	
31	`exploration/ife_e2e/generated/` regenerated live (syside license) from
32	`exploration/ife_e2e/models/` against sysml-codegen's `constraint-exec-epic` branch (W1
33	landed): 8 modules (was 6 pre-epic), including the new
34	`HifPlantViabilityConstraintModule` and `ConstraintReportAggregatorModule`. Sealed
35	(`contracts/{model_contract,package_contract,verify}.py`). Anchors A/B/C in `run_anchors.py`
36	all re-verified byte-exact against the pre-existing acceptance numbers (memory
37	`item3-fusiontea-acceptance-facts`): LCOE $252.29996307 / $68.69020165 / $270.12117794,
38	Meier COE 4.735 c/kWh — the regeneration changed nothing about the plant's numerics, only
39	added the now-executing constraint.
40	
41	`run_anchors.py` needed two small, harness-side fixes to keep working now that the
42	whole-plant package's ExitPoint carries constraint evidence for the first time (a real,
43	expected side effect of W1 landing, not a design problem): the router needs a write handler
44	for every `CUSTOM_SCHEMA_TYPES` entry (was hardcoded to `["RootModel[float]"]` only), and the
45	anchor-comparison dict must skip non-numeric ExitPoint outputs (`ConstraintEvaluation`/
46	`ConstraintReport`) instead of blindly `float()`-coercing every channel.
47	
48	## Three named schema/wiring gaps (surfacing — not silently patched around)
49	
50	**Preconditions were reported "ALL MET"** (W1 landed, teax Items 10-12 certified, W5b loader
51	seal wired) — true for the single-entry-channel toy fixture every teax test and the pre-Item-9
52	Item-0 spike (`teax/.project/active/constraint-study-integration-spike/`) exercised. This
53	session is the first time a *real, multi-entry-channel, whole-plant* sysml-codegen package has
54	been run through the certified teax study layer, and it surfaced three gaps the certifications
55	didn't catch. None are architectural — each is exactly the "schema/naming/wiring" class the
56	Item-0 spike's own mismatches were. All three were bridged from fusion-tea's side only
57	(sysml-codegen and teax source are out of this session's sandbox); each bridge is a small,
58	clearly-marked adapter, not a silent workaround:
59	
60	1. **`contracts/constraint_catalog.json` is never emitted as a standalone file.**
61	   sysml-codegen's Item 9 embeds the constraint catalog inside `contracts/model_contract.json`
62	   (key `constraint_catalog`), with field names (`usage_qualified_name`,
63	   `definition_qualified_name`, `formal_names`) that don't match what teax's Item 12
64	   (`simkit.study.config`, `simkit.study.cli`, `simkit.study.query._Catalog`) reads from a
65	   *standalone* `contracts/constraint_catalog.json` (`usage_name`, `source_usage`, `owner_qn`,
66	   `definition_qn`, `source_form`). teax's own fixture at
67	   `teax/packages/teax-simkit/simkit/tests/evaluation/fixtures/sealed_package/package_live/
68	   contracts/constraint_catalog.json` is hand-authored to teax's expected shape — it was never
69	   generated by, or checked against, a real sysml-codegen Item 9 artifact until this session.
70	   **Bridge:** `materialize_constraint_catalog.py` derives a conformant standalone file from
71	   the embedded catalog, then `sysml-codegen seal` re-seals the package so the derived file is
72	   covered by the integrity hash set (the same `seal` command the CLI documents for
73	   "after editing a handwritten stencil").
74	2. **`CandidateBridge` only ever builds ONE entry channel's typed model**
75	   (`simkit.study.bridge.CandidateBridge.build`), but `MappingEntrySource.validate`
76	   (`simkit.evaluation.entry_source`) requires *every* channel the package's `EntryPoint`
77	   declares or raises `EvaluationFailed(ENTRY_VALIDATION)` → `StudyBridgeDefect`. The toy
78	   fixture Items 10-12 were built and tested against has exactly one entry channel; this
79	   package's whole-plant `EntryPoint` has four (`hif_driver_params`, `hif_plant_params`,
80	   `ife_plant_params`, `system_design`). This is the same class of gap the Item-0 spike
81	   flagged as mismatch #1 ("Item 10 must define the typed-entry contract at both levels") —
82	   resolved for the single-channel case only. **Bridge:** `MultiChannelEvaluator` in
83	   `run_viability_study.py` wraps the real `PreparedEvaluator`; on every `evaluate()` call it
84	   merges the swept channel (built by the real, unmodified `CandidateBridge`) with the other
85	   three channels' typed models, loaded once from the package's own committed `inputs/*.json`
86	   templates. `StudyRunner`/`CandidateBridge`/`PreparedEvaluator` are unmodified — this plugs
87	   into the documented `Evaluator` protocol seam, the same seam the Item-0 spike proved
88	   pluggable by construction.
89	3. **`PreparedEvaluator.__init__` unconditionally sets `self.ToyPlantParams =
90	   self.package.ToyPlantParams`** (`simkit/evaluation/evaluator.py:107`) — a toy-fixture
91	   convenience left in the constructor, not generalized to the loaded package's actual entry
92	   model name. Any package without a class literally named `ToyPlantParams` fails to
93	   construct. **Bridge:** both driver scripts alias `module.ToyPlantParams =
94	   module.IfePlantParams` on the loaded module before constructing `PreparedEvaluator` —
95	   harmless, additive, no teax source touched.
96	
97	**Recommendation for Phase 6 / a future item:** gaps 1 and 2 are load-bearing for any
98	multi-constraint or multi-entry-channel package (i.e. any real plant model past a toy
99	fixture) — not fusion-tea-specific. They should become real sysml-codegen/teax work items
100	(emit a conformant standalone catalog file; make `CandidateBridge`/`StudyDefinition` carry a
101	full typed-entry set, not one channel) rather than staying as three per-consumer harness
102	adapters. Gap 3 is a one-line fix in teax. None of the three block this item's own
103	Critical Success Factor — the acceptance table and benchmark above are real, and match the
104	epic's expectation — but they mean the "Items 9-12 certified" claim only covers what those
105	items' own test fixtures exercised, not a real whole-plant package until now.
106	
107	## Files
108	
109	- `materialize_constraint_catalog.py` — bridges gap 1 (run before `run_viability_study.py`
110	  if the package is regenerated fresh; already applied to `../generated/`).
111	- `run_viability_study.py` — builds the grid `StudyDefinition`, runs it through the real,
112	  unmodified `StudyRunner`/`StudyStore`/`ObjectivePolicy`, queries verdicts via `StudyQuery`,
113	  writes `acceptance_table.csv`.
114	- `bench_prepare_once.py` — the prepare-once-vs-rebuild benchmark, writes
115	  `prepare_once_benchmark.json`.
116	- `acceptance_table.csv`, `prepare_once_benchmark.json` — committed evidence.
117	- `_work/`, `__pycache__/` — gitignored scratch (SQLite store, artifacts).
118	
119	## Reproduce
120	
121	```bash
122	# from ~/1cfe/fusion-tea
123	cd exploration/ife_e2e/study
124	PYTHONPATH=/home/reid/1cfe/teax/packages/teax-simkit ../../../.venv/bin/python \

1	"""Bridge sysml-codegen's embedded constraint catalog to teax's expected file (W4).
2	
3	**Named schema gap (Appendix C surfacing, not a silent workaround):** sysml-codegen's Item 9
4	seals a package with the constraint catalog EMBEDDED in ``contracts/model_contract.json``
5	(the ``constraint_catalog`` key — see ``ConstraintCatalog`` in
6	``sysml_codegen.contracts.models``). teax's Item 12 (``simkit.study.config``,
7	``simkit.study.cli``, ``simkit.study.query._Catalog``) reads a STANDALONE
8	``contracts/constraint_catalog.json``, with different field names
9	(``usage_name``/``source_usage``/``owner_qn``/``definition_qn``/``source_form`` vs.
10	sysml-codegen's ``usage_qualified_name``/``definition_qualified_name``/``formal_names``).
11	teax's own fixture at
12	``teax/packages/teax-simkit/simkit/tests/evaluation/fixtures/sealed_package/package_live/
13	contracts/constraint_catalog.json`` is hand-authored to the shape teax's Item 12 code
14	expects — it was never validated against a real sysml-codegen Item 9 artifact, and this is
15	the first time the two sides have been run against each other. Item 9 and Item 12 do NOT
16	interoperate as-is. This script is fusion-tea's harness-side bridge — it does not touch
17	sysml-codegen or teax source (both out of this session's sandbox), so this repo's copy of
18	Appendix C can still "route the sweep through the study layer" as specified. The mismatch
19	itself is recorded for the Phase-6 reconcile, not papered over.
20	
21	Only one field is genuinely synthesized (not renamed/copied): ``source_form`` is set to the
22	literal ``"definition_typed"`` for every record, since every constraint usage this repo's
23	models emit is of that form (``assert constraint <name> : '<Def>' { ... }`` — a usage typed
24	by a constraint definition). sysml-codegen's Item 9 output carries no explicit source-form
25	field to copy from.
26	
27	Run:  uv run python exploration/ife_e2e/study/materialize_constraint_catalog.py <package_dir>
28	"""
29	
30	from __future__ import annotations
31	
32	import json
33	import sys
34	from pathlib import Path
35	
36	
37	def materialize(package_dir: Path) -> Path:
38	    model_contract = json.loads((package_dir / "contracts" / "model_contract.json").read_text())
39	    embedded = model_contract["constraint_catalog"]
40	    if embedded is None:
41	        raise ValueError(f"{package_dir}: model_contract.json carries no constraint_catalog")
42	
43	    # source_records: sysml-codegen keys by definition; teax keys by usage. This package's
44	    # catalog carries exactly one usage per definition today (no def reused by two usages),
45	    # so the definition's own short name search below is unambiguous; a future model with a
46	    # shared constraint def used by multiple usages would need real usage-level source data
47	    # sysml-codegen does not currently emit (a second, larger gap this bridge cannot close).
48	    source_by_def_qn = {r["definition_qualified_name"]: r for r in embedded["source_records"]}
49	
50	    out_source_records = []
51	    out_concrete_entries = []
52	    for entry in embedded["concrete_entries"]:
53	        usage_qn = entry["usage_qualified_name"]
54	        usage_name = usage_qn.rsplit("::", 1)[-1]
55	        owner_qn = usage_qn.rsplit("::", 1)[0]
56	
57	        # Recover which definition this usage was typed by via the predicate_ir's own
58	        # definition-scoped qualified names (every feature_ref target_qn shares the
59	        # definition's QN prefix) rather than assuming a 1:1 def<->usage order.
60	        definition_qn = None
61	        for def_qn in source_by_def_qn:
62	            if f"{def_qn}::" in entry["predicate_ir"]:
63	                definition_qn = def_qn
64	                break
65	        if definition_qn is None:
66	            raise ValueError(f"cannot recover definition for usage {usage_qn!r}")
67	        src = source_by_def_qn[definition_qn]
68	
69	        out_source_records.append({
70	            "usage_name": usage_name,
71	            "source_form": "definition_typed",
72	            "membership_kind": entry["membership_kind"] or "assert",
73	            "is_negated": entry["is_negated"],
74	            "owner_qn": owner_qn,
75	            "definition_qn": definition_qn,
76	            "predicate_ir": entry["predicate_ir"],
77	            "source_location": None,
78	        })
79	        out_concrete_entries.append({
80	            "constraint_id": entry["constraint_id"],
81	            "source_usage": usage_name,
82	            "owner_instance": entry["owner_instance_path"],
83	            "membership_kind": entry["membership_kind"] or "assert",
84	            "is_negated": entry["is_negated"],
85	            "expected_value": entry["expected_value"],
86	        })
87	
88	    catalog = {"source_records": out_source_records, "concrete_entries": out_concrete_entries}
89	    out_path = package_dir / "contracts" / "constraint_catalog.json"
90	    out_path.write_text(json.dumps(catalog, indent=2) + "\n")
91	    return out_path
92	
93	
94	if __name__ == "__main__":
95	    written = materialize(Path(sys.argv[1]))
96	    print(f"wrote {written}")

1	"""Compiled Kleene predicates (Item 7 / D2/D3) — one function per constraint definition.
2	
3	Compile-once, class-per-assertion (INV-1): every constraint module instantiated from the same
4	source assertion imports its function from here rather than duplicating the compiled predicate.
5	"""
6	
7	import math
8	from typing import NamedTuple
9	
10	
11	class _PredicateResult(NamedTuple):
12	    actual_value: object  # True/False/None (None = indeterminate)
13	    status: str           # satisfied | violated | indeterminate
14	    margin: object         # signed float or None (simple-inequality roots only)
15	
16	
17	def _fin(x):
18	    return isinstance(x, (int, float)) and math.isfinite(x)
19	
20	
21	def _cmp(op, a, b):
22	    """Leaf comparison: unknown (None) if either operand is non-finite."""
23	    if not _fin(a) or not _fin(b):
24	        return None
25	    if op == "<=": return a <= b
26	    if op == ">=": return a >= b

15	# (generated/handwritten/mfe_plasma_scaling/dt_fusion_power_impl.py). The

18	N_INTERVALS = 200_000

21	def _sigv_dt(T_keV):
22	    """Bosch-Hale D-T reactivity <sigma*v> [m^3/s] (reactivity.py:54-70)."""
23	    T = max(T_keV, 1e-6)
24	    theta = T / (
25	        1.0
26	        - T * (1.51361e-2 + T * (4.60643e-3 + T * -1.06750e-4))
27	        / (1.0 + T * (7.51886e-2 + T * (1.35000e-2 + T * 1.36600e-5)))
28	    )
29	    xi = ((34.3827 * 34.3827) / (4.0 * theta)) ** (1.0 / 3.0)
30	    return (
31	        1.17302e-9 * theta
32	        * math.sqrt(xi / (1124656.0 * T * T * T))
33	        * math.exp(-3.0 * xi) * 1e-6
34	    )

37	def _profile_integral(alpha_n, alpha_T, T_i0):
38	    """I = trapezoid_{rho in [0,1]} (1-rho^2)^(2*alpha_n) * sigv_dt(T_i0*(1-rho^2)^alpha_T) * 2*rho."""
39	    acc = 0.0
40	    n = N_INTERVALS
41	    for i in range(n + 1):
42	        rho = i / n
43	        u = 1.0 - rho * rho
44	        f = (u ** (2.0 * alpha_n)) * _sigv_dt(T_i0 * (u ** alpha_T)) * 2.0 * rho
45	        acc += f if 0 < i < n else 0.5 * f
46	    return acc / n

120	def compute():
121	    p = IN
122	    # --- Plasma Geometry ---
123	    V = 2.0 * (p["pi"] ** 2) * p["R"] * (p["a"] ** 2) * p["kappa"] * p["f_shape"]
124	    # --- MFE Radial Build (WI-021; geometry.py torus branch) ---
125	    vacuum_or = p["a"] + p["vacuum_t"]
126	    firstwall_or = vacuum_or + p["firstwall_t"]
127	    blanket_or = firstwall_or + p["blanket_t"]
128	    reflector_or = blanket_or + p["reflector_t"]
129	    ht_shield_or = reflector_or + p["ht_shield_t"]
130	    structure_or = ht_shield_or + p["structure_t"]
131	    gap1_or = structure_or + p["gap1_t"]
132	    vessel_or = gap1_or + p["vessel_t"]
133	    coil_or = vessel_or + p["coil_t"]
134	    gap2_or = coil_or + p["gap2_t"]
135	    lt_shield_or = gap2_or + p["lt_shield_t"]
136	    C = p["kappa"] * 2.0 * (p["pi"] ** 2) * p["R"]
137	    firstwall_vol = C * ((firstwall_or ** 2) - (vacuum_or ** 2))
138	    blanket_layer_vol = C * ((blanket_or ** 2) - (firstwall_or ** 2))
139	    reflector_vol = C * ((reflector_or ** 2) - (blanket_or ** 2))
140	    ht_shield_vol = C * ((ht_shield_or ** 2) - (reflector_or ** 2))
141	    lt_shield_vol = C * ((lt_shield_or ** 2) - (gap2_or ** 2))
142	    blanket_vol = firstwall_vol + blanket_layer_vol + reflector_vol
143	    shield_vol = ht_shield_vol + lt_shield_vol
144	    structure_vol = C * ((structure_or ** 2) - (ht_shield_or ** 2))
145	    vessel_vol = C * ((vessel_or ** 2) - (gap1_or ** 2))
146	    wall_area = p["kappa"] * 4.0 * (p["pi"] ** 2) * p["R"] * vacuum_or
147	    r_coil = vessel_or
148	    # CAS27 PbLi inventory keyed to the computed blanket volume (WI-021)
149	    special_materials_capital = blanket_vol * 0.50 * 9400.0 * 5.0
150	    # --- DT Fusion Power (WI-022: 0D bypass or profile-integrated) ---
151	    if p["sigma_v"] > 0.0:
152	        p_fus = 0.25 * (p["n_e"] ** 2) * p["sigma_v"] * p["E_fus"] * V * 1.0e-6
153	    else:
154	        integral = _profile_integral(p["alpha_n"], p["alpha_T"], p["T_i0"])
155	        p_fus = p["n_D0"] * p["n_T0"] * integral * p["E_fus"] * V * 1.0e-6
156	    # --- MFE Power Balance (WI-019 faithful form; physics.py:290-328) ---
157	    p_alpha = (3.52 / 17.58) * p_fus
158	    p_neutron = p_fus - p_alpha
159	    p_cool = p["p_tfcool"] + p["p_pfcool"]
160	    p_aux = p["p_trit"] + p["p_house"]
161	    p_coils = p["p_tf"] + p["p_pf"]
162	    p_th = (p["mn"] * p_neutron + p_alpha + p["p_input"]
163	            + p["eta_p"] * p["p_pump"])
164	    p_the = p["eta_th"] * p_th
165	    p_et = p_the
166	    p_sub = p["f_sub"] * p_et
167	    # Cryoplant electrical chain (WI-024) — mirrors the generated
168	    # cryoplant_electrical_power_impl.py statement forms verbatim (bit-exact):
169	    cop_carnot = (p["T_cold_cryo"] / (p["T_amb_cryo"] - p["T_cold_cryo"]))
170	    cop = (p["f_carnot_cryo"] * cop_carnot)
171	    p_cold = ((((p["q_nuc_cryo"] * p["vol_cold_cryo"]) * 1e-06) + p["p_fixed_cryo"]) * p["f_uplift_cryo"])
172	    p_cryo = ((p_cold / cop) + p["p_cryo_direct"])
173	    recirculating = (p_coils + p["p_pump"] + p_sub + p_aux + p_cool + p_cryo
174	                     + p["p_input"] / p["eta_pin"])
175	    q_eng = p_et / recirculating
176	    rec_frac = 1.0 / q_eng
177	    p_net = (1.0 - rec_frac) * p_et
178	
179	    # --- Account costs ($) ---
180	    total_kAm = (p["magnet_G"] * p["magnet_B"] * p["magnet_R0"] * r_coil
181	                 / (p["mu0"] * 1000.0))
182	    magnet = total_kAm * p["magnet_cost_per_kAm"] * p["magnet_coil_markup"]
183	    blanket = (p["blanket_unit_cost"] * p["blanket_structure_factor"] * blanket_vol
184	               * (p_th / p["p_th_ref"]) ** p["alpha_06"])
185	    shield = (p["shield_unit_cost"] * shield_vol * p["shield_scale"]
186	              * (p_th / p["p_th_ref"]) ** p["alpha_06"])
187	    structure = (p["structure_unit_cost"] * structure_vol
188	                 * (p_et / p["p_et_ref"]) ** p["alpha_05"])
189	    vessel = (p["vessel_unit_cost"] * vessel_vol
190	              * (p_et / p["p_et_ref"]) ** p["alpha_06"])
191	    power_supplies = p["power_supplies_base"] * (p_et / p["p_et_ref"]) ** p["alpha_07"]
192	    divertor = p["divertor_base"] * (p_th / p["divertor_p_th_ref"]) ** p["divertor_alpha"]
193	    heating = p["heating_ecrh_per_mw"] * p["p_ecrh"]  # ECRH-only; others zero
194	    turbine = p["n_mod"] * p_the * p["turbine_per_mw"]
195	    electric = p["n_mod"] * p_et * p["electric_per_mw"]
196	    heat_rejection = p["n_mod"] * p_th * p["heat_rej_per_mw"]
197	    misc = p["n_mod"] * p_et * p["misc_per_mw"]
198	
199	    # Forward-computed direct accounts (WI-025) — mirror the generated
200	    # buildings_cost / precon_cost / om_cost impl statement forms verbatim
201	    # (bit-exact); p_the_ref = p_et_ref = 1100 (no DEC), n_mod frozen at 1.
202	    buildings = (((((p["bldg_fixed_base"]
203	        + (p["bldg_fus_base"] * ((p_fus * p["n_mod"]) / p["bldg_p_fus_ref"])))
204	        + (p["bldg_staff_base"] * (((p_et * p["n_mod"]) / p["p_et_ref"]) ** 0.5)))
205	        + (p["bldg_the_base"] * ((p_the * p["n_mod"]) / p["p_et_ref"])))
206	        + (p["bldg_th_base"] * ((p_th * p["n_mod"]) / p["p_th_ref"])))
207	        + (p["bldg_et_base"] * ((p_et * p["n_mod"]) / p["p_et_ref"])))
208	    precon = (((p["land_intensity"] * (((p_net * p["n_mod"]) * p["ref_net_power"]) ** 0.5))
209	               * p["land_cost"]) + p["precon_fixed_base"])
210	    annual_om = ((p["om_annual_ref"] * (((p_net * p["n_mod"]) / p["ref_net_power"]) ** p["om_alpha"]))
211	                 + p["om_direct"])
212	
213	    powercore_capital = (magnet + heating + divertor + blanket + shield
214	                         + structure + vessel + power_supplies)
215	    bop_capital = turbine + electric + heat_rejection + misc
216	    direct_capital = (powercore_capital + bop_capital + buildings
217	                      + precon + special_materials_capital)
218	    contingency_capital = p["contingency_rate"] * direct_capital
219	    indirect_capital = (p["indirect_fraction"] * direct_capital
220	                        * (p["construction_years"] / p["reference_construction_time"]))
221	    total_capital = direct_capital + contingency_capital + indirect_capital
222	
223	    # --- LCOE DCF ($/MWh) ---
224	    d = p["discount_rate"]
225	    N = p["operational_years"]
226	    discount_pow_n = (1.0 + d) ** N
227	    crf = d * discount_pow_n / (discount_pow_n - 1.0)
228	    idc_factor = (1.0 + d) ** (p["construction_years"] / 2.0)
229	    annual_capital = total_capital * idc_factor * crf
230	    annual_energy_mwh = 8760.0 * p_net * p["availability"]
231	    lcoe = (annual_capital + annual_om) / annual_energy_mwh
232	
233	    # --- Neutron wall load ---
234	    wall_load = p_fus * (1.0 - 0.2002) / wall_area
235	
236	    return dict(
237	        V=V, p_fus=p_fus, p_th=p_th, p_the=p_the, p_et=p_et,

240	        magnet=magnet, heating=heating, divertor=divertor, blanket=blanket,
241	        shield=shield, structure=structure, vessel=vessel,
242	        power_supplies=power_supplies, turbine=turbine, electric=electric,
243	        heat_rejection=heat_rejection, misc=misc,
244	        buildings=buildings, precon=precon,  # forward-computed (WI-025)

246	        special_materials=special_materials_capital,
247	        powercore_capital=powercore_capital, bop_capital=bop_capital,
248	        direct_capital=direct_capital, contingency_capital=contingency_capital,
249	        indirect_capital=indirect_capital, total_capital=total_capital, lcoe=lcoe,
250	    )

1	"""WI-015 viability sweep: grid over (eta, G, f) using the GENERATED modules.
2	
3	Calls the codegen-generated implementation functions directly
4	(ife_tea.handwritten.*) — the same code the teax executor ran for the anchor
5	checks — in-process, so a ~10k-point grid takes seconds instead of hours.
6	
7	Classification per point:
8	  - viable: the GENERATED 'Viability Threshold' predicate (eta * gain >= threshold,
9	    threshold default 10.0; fusion_cycle.sysml, DI-001), called directly —
10	    CONSTRAINT-EXEC Item 14 (W1) landed the fix that lets this constraint lower and
11	    execute; W4 retired the harness's hand-duplicated `eta * G > 10` rule (formerly
12	    here) in favor of the model's own assertion. See
13	    `study/run_viability_study.py` for the full acceptance replay (old hand rule vs
14	    this predicate, over the same grid) that authorized the retirement — 100%
15	    agreement except grid points exactly ON the threshold, where the hand rule's
16	    strict `>` and the model's `>=` genuinely diverge (7 such points; flagged, not
17	    reconciled away, in `study/acceptance_table.csv`).
18	  - power_positive: P_net > 0      (Hawker Eq. 2.12: eta_th*M*G*eta > 2)
19	  - attractive:  viable AND lcoe <= $100/MWh (LCOE-threshold overlay; policy,
20	    stays hand-coded — not a modeled constraint)
21	
22	Non-swept parameters are held at the realistic-HIF baseline (anchor B),
23	so the f=5 Hz, eta=0.25, G=100 grid point reproduces the $68.69 anchor.
24	
25	Run:  ../pipeline_spike/.venv-exec/bin/python sweep_ife.py
26	Output: data/ife_sweep/sweep_results.csv
27	"""
28	
29	import csv
30	import sys
31	import time
32	from pathlib import Path
33	
34	E2E = Path(__file__).parent
35	REPO = E2E.parent.parent
36	OUT = REPO / "data/ife_sweep"
37	
38	pkg_dir = E2E / "pkg"
39	sys.path.insert(0, str(pkg_dir))
40	
41	from ife_tea.handwritten.fusion_cycle.recirculating_power_fraction_impl import (  # noqa: E402
42	    run_recirculating_power_fraction,
43	)
44	from ife_tea.handwritten.ife_lcoe.ife_lcoe_impl import run_ife_lcoe  # noqa: E402
45	from ife_tea.modules.constraints.predicates import (  # noqa: E402
46	    constraint_pred_ife_plant__ife_power_plant__viability,
47	)
48	from ife_tea.modules.fusion_cycle.recirculating_power_fraction import (  # noqa: E402
49	    Recirculating_Power_FractionInput,
50	)
51	from ife_tea.modules.ife_lcoe.ife_lcoe import IFE_LCOEInput  # noqa: E402
52	
53	# Realistic-HIF baseline (anchor B) for non-swept parameters
54	BASE = dict(
55	    availability=0.85, blanket_energy_multiple=1.2, discount_rate=0.05,
56	    driver_cost_constant=5.0, driver_energy=5.0e6, driver_lifetime_shots=1.0e9,
57	    om_cost_constant=30.0, plant_cost_constant=3000.0,
58	    target_cost_constant=0.50, thermal_efficiency=0.40,
59	    yield_cost_constant=5.0e6, construction_years=5.0, operational_years=40.0,
60	)
61	
62	ETA_GRID = [0.02 + 0.01 * i for i in range(39)]          # 0.02 .. 0.40
63	G_GRID = [10.0 + 5.0 * i for i in range(59)]             # 10 .. 300
64	F_GRID = [1.0, 2.0, 5.0, 10.0, 20.0]                     # Hz
65	
66	LCOE_THRESHOLD = 100.0    # $/MWh overlay (policy, hand-coded — see module docstring)
67	VIABILITY_THRESHOLD = 10.0  # 'Viability Threshold' constraint default (fusion_cycle.sysml)
68	
69	
70	def main() -> None:
71	    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
72	    t0 = time.time()
73	    rows = []
74	    for f in F_GRID:
75	        for eta in ETA_GRID:
76	            for g in G_GRID:
77	                inp = IFE_LCOEInput(
78	                    driver_efficiency=eta, gain=g, frequency=f, **BASE
79	                )
80	                lcoe = run_ife_lcoe(inp)
81	                f_recirc = run_recirculating_power_fraction(
82	                    Recirculating_Power_FractionInput(
83	                        eta=eta, gain=g,
84	                        blanket_multiplier=BASE["blanket_energy_multiple"],
85	                        thermal_efficiency=BASE["thermal_efficiency"],
86	                    )
87	                )
88	                # P_net > 0 iff eta_th * M * G * eta > 2 (Hawker Eq. 2.12)
89	                p_net_w = (BASE["driver_energy"] * f *
90	                           (BASE["thermal_efficiency"] * BASE["blanket_energy_multiple"]
91	                            * g * eta - 2.0))
92	                eta_g = eta * g
93	                verdict = constraint_pred_ife_plant__ife_power_plant__viability(
94	                    eta=eta, gain=g, threshold=VIABILITY_THRESHOLD
95	                )
96	                viable = verdict.status == "satisfied"
97	                power_positive = p_net_w > 0.0
98	                attractive = viable and power_positive and lcoe <= LCOE_THRESHOLD
99	                rows.append(dict(
100	                    frequency_hz=f, eta=round(eta, 4), gain=g,
101	                    eta_g=round(eta_g, 4),
102	                    lcoe_per_mwh=lcoe if power_positive else float("nan"),
103	                    f_recirc=f_recirc, p_net_mw=p_net_w / 1e6,
104	                    power_positive=power_positive, viable=viable,
105	                    attractive=attractive,
106	                ))
107	
108	    path = OUT / "sweep_results.csv"
109	    with path.open("w", newline="") as fh:
110	        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=list(rows[0].keys()))
111	        w.writeheader()
112	        w.writerows(rows)
113	
114	    n = len(rows)
115	    nv = sum(r["viable"] for r in rows)
116	    na = sum(r["attractive"] for r in rows)
117	    npp = sum(r["power_positive"] for r in rows)
118	    print(f"{n} grid points in {time.time()-t0:.1f}s -> {path}")
119	    print(f"power-positive: {npp} ({100*npp/n:.1f}%)")
120	    print(f"viable ('Viability Threshold' satisfied): {nv} ({100*nv/n:.1f}%)")
121	    print(f"attractive (viable & LCOE<=${LCOE_THRESHOLD:.0f}): {na} ({100*na/n:.1f}%)")
122	
123	    # sanity: anchor B point must be on the grid and reproduce $68.69
124	    hit = [r for r in rows if r["frequency_hz"] == 5.0 and r["eta"] == 0.25
125	           and r["gain"] == 100.0]
126	    assert hit, "anchor B point missing from grid"
127	    lc = hit[0]["lcoe_per_mwh"]
128	    assert abs(lc - 68.6902) < 0.001, f"anchor B on-grid check failed: {lc}"
129	    print(f"on-grid anchor B check: LCOE={lc:.4f} OK")
130	
131	
132	if __name__ == "__main__":
133	    main()
134

153	def set_1cfe_inputs(o):
154	    """Map 1costingFE's merged point onto the generated pipeline inputs.
155	
156	    Money unit: 1costingFE rolls up in M$; the SysML rolls up in $. Every
157	    coefficient 1costingFE stores in M$ (unit costs, per-MW rates, bases) is
158	    fed x1e6 so the SysML produces $. magnet cost_per_kAm ($/kA-m) is fed as-is
159	    (the SysML magnet calc omits the /1e6, so it already yields $).
160	    """
161	    pb = o["pb_params"]
162	    pw = o["power_table"]
163	    uc = o["unit_costs_musd"]
164	    geo = o["geometry"]
165	    rbld = o["radial_build"]  # WI-021: 1cfe's radial-build inputs, fed into rb
166	    coil = o["coil"]
167	    refs = o["refs"]
168	    M = 1e6
169	
170	    # --- fusion-power injection: p_fus is GIVEN by 1costingFE's solve. ---
171	    # Short-circuit the SysML DT Fusion Power calc by choosing sigma_v so the
172	    # geometry x density x reactivity product reproduces 1costingFE's p_fus
173	    # exactly (mapping trap: fusion power is given, not recomputed).
174	    n_e, E_fus = 3.37e20, 2.817e-12
175	    R, a, kappa, pi = coil["R0"], 1.8, 1.6, 3.14159265358979
176	    V = 2.0 * pi**2 * R * a**2 * kappa
177	    p_fus_target = pw["p_fus"]
178	    sigma_v = p_fus_target / (0.25 * n_e**2 * E_fus * V * 1e-6)
179	
180	    eta_pin = o["eta_pin_effective"]
181	
182	    sd = json.loads(SYS_DESIGN.read_text())
183	    sd.update({
184	        # fusion-power injector
185	        f"{P}fusion__n_e": n_e, f"{P}fusion__E_fus": E_fus,
186	        f"{P}fusion__sigma_v": sigma_v,
187	        f"{P}geom__R": R, f"{P}geom__a": a, f"{P}geom__kappa": kappa,
188	        # WI-020: 1costingFE's geometry is a pure elongated torus (no stellarator
189	        # shaping), and the V above (line ~175) is the torus volume. The
190	        # generated params carry the Stellaris instance's shape factor 0.794259,
191	        # so f_shape MUST be overridden to 1.0 here to reproduce 1cfe's torus
192	        # point — otherwise V (and the injected p_fus) is shrunk by 0.794259.
193	        f"{P}geom__f_shape": 1.0,
194	        # WI-021: feed 1costingFE's OWN radial build into the 'MFE Radial Build'
195	        # calc (rb) so it reproduces 1cfe's aggregate material volumes (blanket/
196	        # shield/structure/vessel), first-wall area, and coil bore. rb has its own
197	        # params (rb__*), separate from geom, so the geom__a=1.8 plasma-path
198	        # override above does NOT leak here. This replaces the former direct
199	        # blanket__blanket_vol / ... volume injections (now computed, not settable).
200	        f"{P}rb__R": rbld["R0"], f"{P}rb__a": rbld["plasma_t"], f"{P}rb__kappa": rbld["elon"],
201	        f"{P}rb__vacuum_t": rbld["vacuum_t"], f"{P}rb__firstwall_t": rbld["firstwall_t"],
202	        f"{P}rb__blanket_t": rbld["blanket_t"], f"{P}rb__reflector_t": rbld["reflector_t"],
203	        f"{P}rb__ht_shield_t": rbld["ht_shield_t"], f"{P}rb__structure_t": rbld["structure_t"],
204	        f"{P}rb__gap1_t": rbld["gap1_t"], f"{P}rb__vessel_t": rbld["vessel_t"],
205	        f"{P}rb__coil_t": rbld["coil_t"], f"{P}rb__gap2_t": rbld["gap2_t"],
206	        f"{P}rb__lt_shield_t": rbld["lt_shield_t"],
207	        # power-balance params mapped from 1costingFE merged params
208	        f"{P}pb__p_input": pb["p_input"], f"{P}pb__mn": pb["mn"],
209	        f"{P}pb__eta_th": pb["eta_th"], f"{P}pb__eta_p": pb["eta_p"],
210	        f"{P}pb__eta_pin": eta_pin, f"{P}pb__f_sub": pb["f_sub"],
211	        # WI-019: pumping power is now the same absolute p_pump [MW] input as
212	        # 1costingFE (former fpcppf mapping trap resolved).
213	        f"{P}pb__p_pump": pb["p_pump"],
214	        # SysML splits coils/cooling into tf/pf; 1costingFE has single
215	        # p_coils / p_cool. Put the full 1cfe value in the tf slot, 0 in pf.
216	        f"{P}pb__p_tf": pb["p_coils"], f"{P}pb__p_pf": 0.0,
217	        f"{P}pb__p_tfcool": pb["p_cool"], f"{P}pb__p_pfcool": 0.0,
218	        f"{P}pb__p_trit": pb["p_trit"], f"{P}pb__p_house": pb["p_house"],
219	        # WI-024 (design D7 successor injection): pb__p_cryo is now a
220	        # chain-wired channel, not a settable leaf. Zero the chain's heat
221	        # inputs and feed 1cfe's p_cryo through the additive direct term —
222	        # the identity path is exact in IEEE arithmetic (0-heat chain
223	        # contributes exactly 0; baked f_uplift/T/f_carnot values are inert
224	        # at zero heat), so downstream floats match the pre-WI-024 record
225	        # bit for bit.
226	        f"{P}cryo_elec__q_nuc": 0.0, f"{P}cryo_elec__vol_cold": 0.0,
227	        f"{P}cryo_elec__p_fixed": 0.0, f"{P}cryo_elec__p_direct": pb["p_cryo"],
228	        # heating (ECRH-only for the stellarator point)
229	        f"{P}heating_cost__ecrh_per_mw": uc["heating_ecrh_per_mw"] * M,
230	        f"{P}heating_cost__nbi_per_mw": uc["heating_nbi_per_mw"] * M,
231	        f"{P}heating_cost__icrf_per_mw": 0.0, f"{P}heating_cost__lhcd_per_mw": 0.0,
232	        f"{P}heating_cost__p_ecrh": pb["p_ecrh"], f"{P}heating_cost__p_nbi": 0.0,
233	        f"{P}heating_cost__p_icrf": 0.0, f"{P}heating_cost__p_lhcd": 0.0,
234	        # divertor base
235	        f"{P}divertor_cost__base": uc["divertor_base"] * M,
236	        # rollup rates: 1costingFE point is NOAK -> contingency_rate = 0.
237	        # (The SysML/Stellaris model default is 0.10; fed 0 here to match the
238	        #  1cfe point, footnoted in the report.)
239	        f"{P}contingency__contingency_rate": refs["contingency_rate_noak"],
240	        f"{P}indirect__indirect_fraction": refs["indirect_fraction"],
241	        f"{P}indirect__construction_time": o["target"]["construction_time_yr"],
242	        # WI-025 (design D6 successor injection): lcoe_calc__annual_om is now
243	        # a chain-wired channel (annual_om = om_cost.annual_om), not a
244	        # settable leaf. Zero the O&M reference here so the chain computes
245	        # 0.0*(p_net/1000)^0.5 + om_direct = om_direct — exact in IEEE
246	        # arithmetic (0*finite = 0, 0 + v = v; the WI-024 D7 identity-path
247	        # precedent) — and feed 1cfe's unlevelized annual O&M through the
248	        # additive om_direct term in the params block below, so lcoe receives
249	        # 1cfe's value bit for bit.
250	        f"{P}om_cost__om_ref": 0.0,
251	        # LCOE financing / performance
252	        f"{P}lcoe_calc__availability": o["target"]["availability"],
253	        f"{P}lcoe_calc__construction_years": o["target"]["construction_time_yr"],
254	        f"{P}lcoe_calc__discount_rate": o["target"]["interest_rate"],
255	        f"{P}lcoe_calc__operational_years": float(o["target"]["lifetime_yr"]),
256	    })
257	    SYS_DESIGN.write_text(json.dumps(sd, indent=2))
258	
259	    mp = json.loads(MFE_PARAMS.read_text())
260	    mp.update({
261	        # blanket (C220101). WI-021: blanket_vol is no longer an injectable param
262	        # — it is computed by the 'MFE Radial Build' calc (rb), fed 1cfe's own
263	        # radial build in the sd.update block above, so rb reproduces geo's
264	        # aggregate volumes. Same for shield/structure/vessel volumes and r_coil.
265	        f"{P}blanket__structure_factor": 1.0,  # liquid_metal (PbLi) -> 1.0
266	        f"{P}blanket__unit_cost": uc["blanket_unit_cost_dt"] * M,
267	        f"{P}blanket_cost__alpha": 0.6, f"{P}blanket_cost__p_th_ref": refs["P_TH_REF"],

271	        f"{P}shield_cost__alpha": 0.6, f"{P}shield_cost__p_th_ref": refs["P_TH_REF"],
272	        # structure (C220105)
273	        f"{P}structure__unit_cost": uc["structure_unit_cost"] * M,
274	        f"{P}structure_cost__alpha": 0.5,
275	        f"{P}structure_cost__p_et_ref": refs["ref_gross_power_mwe"],
276	        # vessel (C220106_vessel — shell term only)

279	        f"{P}vessel_cost__p_et_ref": refs["ref_gross_power_mwe"],

285	        f"{P}divertor_cost__alpha": 0.5, f"{P}divertor_cost__p_th_ref": 1000.0,
286	        # magnet (C220103): B <- b_center (NOT radiation B); r_coil now from rb.
287	        f"{P}magnet__B": coil["b_center"], f"{P}magnet__G": coil["G_8pi2"],
288	        f"{P}magnet__R0": coil["R0"], f"{P}magnet__coil_markup": coil["coil_markup"],
289	        f"{P}magnet__cost_per_kAm": coil["cost_per_kam"],

328	def sysml_account_formula(name, o, p_th, p_et):
329	    """Recompute a SysML powercore account with GIVEN thermal/gross power, in $.
330	
331	    Mirrors the generated calc def line-for-line. Used for the formula-isolation
332	    check: fed 1costingFE's OWN p_th/p_et it must reproduce 1costingFE's account
333	    to floating point (proving the formula/codegen is faithful and that the
334	    end-to-end gap is caused by the power-balance inputs, not the cost formula).
335	    """
336	    uc, geo, coil, refs = (o["unit_costs_musd"], o["geometry"], o["coil"], o["refs"])
337	    M = 1e6
338	    et_ref, th_ref = refs["ref_gross_power_mwe"], refs["P_TH_REF"]
339	    if name == "magnet":
340	        mu0 = 1.25663706212e-06
341	        total_kAm = coil["G_8pi2"] * coil["b_center"] * coil["R0"] * geo["r_coil_vessel_or"] / (mu0 * 1000.0)
342	        return total_kAm * coil["cost_per_kam"] * coil["coil_markup"]
343	    if name == "heating":
344	        return uc["heating_ecrh_per_mw"] * M * o["pb_params"]["p_ecrh"]
345	    if name == "blanket":
346	        return uc["blanket_unit_cost_dt"] * M * 1.0 * geo["blanket_vol"] * (p_th / th_ref) ** 0.6
347	    if name == "shield":
348	        return uc["shield_unit_cost"] * M * geo["shield_vol"] * refs["shield_scale_dt"] * (p_th / th_ref) ** 0.6
349	    if name == "structure":
350	        return uc["structure_unit_cost"] * M * geo["structure_vol"] * (p_et / et_ref) ** 0.5
351	    if name == "vessel":
352	        return uc["vessel_unit_cost"] * M * geo["vessel_vol"] * (p_et / et_ref) ** 0.6
353	    if name == "power_supplies":
354	        return uc["power_supplies_base"] * M * (p_et / et_ref) ** 0.7
355	    if name == "divertor":
356	        return uc["divertor_base"] * M * (p_th / 1000.0) ** 0.5
357	    raise KeyError(name)

361	    d = max(abs(a), abs(b), 1e-30)
362	    return (a - b) / d

4	topic: "Code review of the open PR wave: sysml-codegen #9 (constraint-exec-epic @ 512786c) and agentic-mbse #11 (@ 54a95d2)"
5	tags: [research, code-review, constraint-exec, gap-close, pr-wave]
6	status: complete

8	---
9	
10	# Research: Open-PR Code Review — CONSTRAINT-EXEC Wave (#9, #11)
11	
12	**Research Question:** general code bugs, gaps, and software-quality issues on the open PR branches,
13	beyond the already-filed findings (F1–F10 gap review, `[CONSTRAINT-ARCH-UNIFY]`,
14	`[ANON-ELIGIBLE-KEY]`, `[EXIT-PIN-SEAM]`, mypy baseline).
15	
16	**Scope reviewed:** PR #9 src diff (42 files, ~4.9k insertions: analysis, generation + templates,
17	resolution/contracts/snapshot, CLI/orchestration/extraction) plus a test-quality sample of the
18	largest new test files; PR #11 src diff (11 files, ~2.7k insertions) at the pushed ref `54a95d2`.
19	Five reviewers, each instructed to verify findings concretely before reporting; "reproduced" below
20	means an executed reproduction, "traced" means a concrete code-path trace without execution.
21	
22	## Summary
23	
24	- **Four High findings, all in territory no prior review wave covered.** Two are wrong-verdict
25	  defects in the v3 executable profile (ordering comparisons admit non-numeric operands; negated
26	  asserts silently invert), one is a silent-evidence family in generated code (model formal names
27	  shadowing generated locals), one crashes from-snapshot rebuild on a valid snapshot (nullable-QN
28	  ADMIT filter).
29	- The Highs share one systematic shape: **a fact the schema deliberately captures that the decision
30	  or generation layer never consults** (operand category under ordering; `is_negated`; the generated
31	  scope's own names; anonymous identity in the demand collector). Guards check validity, not
32	  collision with the system's own machinery.
33	- Medium findings cluster at the **portability and diagnostic-fidelity seams**: named excluded
34	  locations leak absolute machine paths into fingerprints and contracts; recursive part containment
35	  silently truncates; a constraint demand can overwrite a calc-usage-derived design attribute's
36	  grouping; seal can produce packages that can never verify; the v3 loader breaks its own
37	  "never a raw KeyError" promise.
38	- **Overall quality is high.** Every reviewer independently reported disciplined work: fail-fast over
39	  fallback, real invariant guards firing before writes, deterministic ordering at every iteration
40	  point checked, correct Kleene semantics, byte-stable codecs, and an unusually strong test wave
41	  (hand-written literals, executed predicates, mutation pins). The defects below are the residue at
42	  seams the discipline didn't reach, not a pattern of sloppiness.
43	
44	## High findings (recommend fixing before the wave merges)
45	
46	### R-1 — Ordering comparisons admit non-numeric operand categories (PR #11) — reproduced live
47	`agentic-mbse src/agentic_mbse/sysml/executable_profile.py:521-525` (`_walk_comparison` ordering
48	branch); root cause `unit_compatibility` at `:164-195`.
49	The ordering path (`<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`) gates only on `unit_compatibility`, which returns `"ok"`
50	for any pair of non-quantity categories. The category guards exist only in `classify_equality`.
51	Reproduced end-to-end via live syside extraction: `assert constraint { label1 < label2 }` (String
52	attrs) and `assert constraint { armed <= ready }` (Boolean attrs) both return **ADMIT with zero
53	diagnostics** — a string/boolean/enum ordering enters codegen as an executable numerical claim.
54	The golden matrix pins only two inequality rows (quantity/quantity, integer/real), so no test sees
55	this. This is an admit-by-fallthrough hole in a default-deny profile — the exact defect class v3
56	exists to prevent.
57	
58	### R-2 — `is_negated` is captured but never consulted: negated asserts admit inverted (PR #11) — reproduced live
59	`agentic-mbse src/agentic_mbse/sysml/executable_profile.py:717-783` (`_evaluate_usage` reads only
60	form/identity/location/predicate); `ConstraintUsageFact.is_negated` populated at
61	`constraint_extraction.py:688`.
62	`assert not constraint { width < 5.0 }` extracts cleanly with `is_negated=True`; the profile ADMITs
63	with `effective_predicate` = the positive IR and no diagnostics. `effective_predicate` is exactly
64	what codegen lowers, and `UsageDecision` carries no negation flag, so the generated check asserts
65	the inverse of the model. Should at minimum be a named BLOCK, or fold the negation into the IR.
66	
67	### R-3 — Reserved-name shadowing family in generated code (PR #9) — reproduced by executing generated code
68	`src/sysml_codegen/generation/predicate_compiler.py:260-271` and
69	`src/sysml_codegen/templates/constraint_module.py.jinja2:32-42`. Guards check model-derived formal
70	names only for `isidentifier()`/`iskeyword()`, never for colliding with the generated code's own
71	scope names. Three symptoms, one seam:
72	- **Formal named `value`** (natural: `in value : Real`): the emitted body rebinds local `value` (the
73	  verdict) before the margin expression re-reads the leaf → margin evidence silently corrupted,
74	  including a violated constraint reporting a **positive** margin (sign inversion). Formal named
75	  `status` → margin silently `None`. Verdict stays correct; only the evidence is wrong — the silent
76	  kind. (High)
77	- **Formal named `verdict`**: template rebinds the run parameter, then `float(verdict)` on a
78	  `_PredicateResult` → generated module raises `TypeError` on every run, violating INV-3 from a
79	  valid model. (Medium)
80	- **Formal named `self`**: `def run(self, self: float)` → `SyntaxError`; generation succeeds
81	  silently, failure surfaces at import. (Medium)
82	Fix shape: a deny-list-plus-rename at the sanitize or compile seam covers all three.
83	
84	### R-4 — Nullable-QN ADMIT filter crashes from-snapshot rebuild on a valid snapshot (PR #9) — reproduced
85	`src/sysml_codegen/analysis/constraint_lowering.py:448-459` (`collect_bare_actual_demand`).
86	`admit_qns` is a set of `identity.qualified_name`; anonymous usages have `qualified_name=None`, so
87	one anonymous ADMIT usage inserts `None` and every anonymous **excluded** usage then passes the
88	`not in admit_qns` filter and gets owner-expanded. Live capture succeeds (the excluded branch never
89	queries that owner, so the frozen transcript omits it); from-snapshot rebuild then raises
90	`FrozenOccurrenceIndexCorruptionError` — not in the `except` tuple at `:459` — with a misleading
91	"recapture the snapshot" message. Live-side, the same mismatch mints spurious synthesized
92	supplied-value attributes for constraints that never execute. Note: this re-imports the same
93	nullable-QN identity mistake F5 just fixed elsewhere in the file (`excluded_usage_indices` already
94	uses positional zip for exactly this reason). Also missing: the owner-kind filter — an ADMIT usage
95	with an out-of-profile owner falls into `_expand_owner_instances`'s "never reached" package branch.
96	
97	## Medium findings
98	
99	### R-5 — Recursive part containment silently truncates the occurrence set (PR #9) — reproduced
100	`src/sysml_codegen/analysis/part_instance_index.py:158-161`. The `_visited` cycle guard returns `[]`
101	for a revisited definition, so `part def A { part suba : A; }` + `part a1 : A;` yields only the
102	non-recursive occurrences — no `NonFiniteCardinalityError`, no diagnostic. Violates the module's
103	own INV-2 ("no third disposition beyond expand-finite or block-loud") and lower_constraints'
104	one-record-per-instance INV-3: a part_def-owned assert lowers to one concrete constraint and the
105	nested instances are silently never checked. Correct behavior per design: loud block, matching the
106	`[*]` multiplicity path.
107	
108	### R-6 — Named excluded locations leak absolute machine paths into fingerprints and contracts (PR #9) — reproduced end-to-end
109	Found independently by two reviewers. `src/sysml_codegen/snapshot/serializer.py:145-159`
110	canonicalizes `location.file` only for anonymous excluded usages; `constraint_lowering.py:496-508`
111	(`_exclusion_for`/`_render_location`) keeps the raw parser path for named excluded usages. The raw
112	path flows into `excluded_records` → `catalog.fingerprint` → `semantic_fingerprint` and
113	`contracts/model_contract.json`, and is rendered into the generated `report_aggregator.py`.
114	Reproduced: `generate --from-snapshot tests/fixtures/constraint_non_numerical/extraction_snapshot.json`
115	emits a contract containing `"location": "///home/reid/1cfe/sysml-codegen/tests/fixtures/..."`.
116	Consequences: local paths ship inside generated packages; regenerating the same model from another
117	checkout changes package bytes solely through the fingerprint; live-vs-snapshot parity holds only on
118	the capture machine. The committed fixture snapshot already carries the `/home/reid` path.
119	
120	### R-7 — Constraint-actual demand silently overwrites a calc-usage-derived synthesized design attribute (PR #9) — reproduced
121	`src/sysml_codegen/resolution/supplied_values.py:265-268` appends constraint demand entries after
122	calc-usage entries with no dedupe, and `collect_bare_actual_demand` collects every ADMIT
123	feature-reference actual, not only bare ones as its name and the D2 docstring promise. When the same
124	`(instance_scope, source_path)` resolves via both routes, the later constraint entry overwrites
125	`synth[target.qn]` (`:299-312`), replacing `source_file` with the constraint's file — so a model
126	that keeps assertions in a separate `.sysml` file regroups that entry point into the constraint
127	file's parameter group (different schema/inputs JSON) the moment lowering is enabled. Side effects:
128	`scanned`/`applied` double-count; the REQ-SVM-03 collision warning can fire twice.
129	
130	### R-8 — The F4 warning pre-pass can itself halt, masking the BLOCK diagnostic (PR #9) — reproduced
131	`src/sysml_codegen/analysis/constraint_lowering.py:549-550, :565, :591`
132	(`_report_non_numerical_warnings` → `_warning_location` → `_canonical_anonymous_location`).
133	If an anonymous NON_NUMERICAL statement's file maps to no model root (e.g. an imported library
134	outside `--models`), the pre-pass raises "raw source '...' does not match any supplied model root":
135	zero warnings are emitted and the actionable BLOCK halt (constraint name, reason, repair text) is
136	replaced. The F4 warnings-before-halt guarantee is conditional on referent mapping succeeding.
137	Reachability from live extraction unproven; the failure mode is real. (Found during the GAP-CLOSE
138	Item 2 independent audit.)
139	
140	### R-9 — `_literal_float` silently loses signed and unit-annotated modeled defaults (PR #9) — reproduced at unit level
141	`src/sysml_codegen/analysis/constraint_lowering.py:1114-1124`; consequence
142	`generation/entry_point.py:272-273`. Only a bare `LiteralNode` yields a value: `:= -0.1`
143	(unary-minus OperatorNode — the shape the profile's unary-sign support exists for) and `= 40.0 [MW]`
144	(UnitAnnotationNode) return `None`, so the MODELED_DEFAULT formal mints a LIBRARY_DEFAULT entry
145	point with `default_value=None` and the generated JSON input omits the key — a default the model
146	explicitly carries becomes a value the user must re-supply.
147	
148	### R-10 — Seal/verify symlink gaps: seal produces unverifiable packages; dangling symlinks pass verify (PR #9) — reproduced
149	Found independently by two reviewers.
150	- `src/sysml_codegen/contracts/seal.py:67-73` has no symlink policy: sealing a tree containing an
151	  escaping file symlink records and hashes it; a directory symlink is silently skipped. Both produce
152	  a "successfully sealed" package that immediately fails its own verification (`INVALID_PATH`) —
153	  the failure surfaces at first load, far from the cause, with no diagnostic at seal time
154	  (`cli/__init__.py:610-640` Step 9 completes without error).
155	- `src/sysml_codegen/contracts/verify.py:277-307`: a dangling symlink is neither dir-symlink nor
156	  file, so the extras walk skips it with no diagnostic — `ok=True`. It is uncovered mutable content
157	  (live the moment its target exists), the same threat class F9 closed.
158	
159	### R-11 — v3 loader violates its own "never a raw KeyError" gate on malformed section shapes (PR #9) — reproduced
160	`src/sysml_codegen/snapshot/loader.py:154-199` gates only presence and `schema_version`.
161	`part_occurrences` as a list → raw `AttributeError` (via `part_instance_index.py:425-447`); an
162	occurrence missing `steps` → bare `KeyError: 'steps'`; `constraint_facts.usages = 42` → bare
163	`TypeError`. None carry the re-capture instruction the loader's comment (`:154-156`) promises for
164	every v3 section.
165	
166	### R-12 — Explicitly-set but invalid `TEAX_SIMKIT_PATH` silently falls through to the sibling (PR #9, test infra) — reproduced
167	`tests/helpers/teax_discovery.py:12-38`. An operator pinning a specific simkit build who typos the
168	path (or whose checkout moves) silently validates against `../teax/packages/teax-simkit` instead —
169	green results against the wrong dependency. The dangerous cell (invalid explicit + valid sibling) is
170	exactly the one `tests/unit/test_teax_discovery.py` doesn't test. An explicitly-set-but-invalid path
171	should be an error or a loud warning. Ironic note: this helper is itself the GAP-CLOSE hygiene fix.
172	
173	## Low / latent / informational
174	
175	**PR #9 production:**
176	- `orchestration/pipeline_builder.py:1004-1009` — load-bearing comment claims
177	  `assemble_constraint_catalog` "returns None when every concrete record is unassessed"; it never
178	  returns None (found independently by two reviewers). Same drift in the
179	  `extend_graph_with_constraints` docstring (`constraint_lowering.py:1153-1155`, "when at least one
180	  assertion is eligible" vs unconditional D11 emission).
181	- `orchestration/pipeline_builder.py:912-930` — P2 constraint-root injection round-trips the resolved
182	  channel through `"{instance_name}.{output}"`; downstream resolves by bare instance name first-wins,
183	  so with `include_all=False` and duplicate instance names the root can anchor to the wrong usage.
184	  Inert on the CLI path (`include_all=True`).
185	- `generation/registry.py:~293-300` — mixes `/` and `.` separators; any future 3-segment
186	  `module_type` emits a SyntaxError import. Unreachable today.
187	- `constraint_lowering.py:972-974` — duplicate actual names last-wins on the inline path where the
188	  definition-typed twin raises (plausible-only; shape may not survive extraction).
189	- `constraint_lowering.py:371-380` vs `analysis/parameter_groups.py:358-367` — opposite duplicate-QN
190	  precedence (last-wins vs first-wins) between the two design-attribute indexes; resolution and
191	  minted `default_value` can come from different records (plausible-only).
192	- `generation/modules.py` `compile_shared_predicates` — `is_negated` read from the first entry with
193	  no cross-entry agreement check; mutation-only (one usage per key under the profile), but it is the
194	  one field the INV-2 guard family doesn't cover.
195	- `generation/predicate_compiler.py:130-135` — n-ary `**` left-folds (wrong associativity);

9	
10	# Research: Constraint Profile Semantics and License Reconciliation
11	
12	## Research Question
13	
14	Did prior owner decisions already determine R-1 non-numeric ordering and R-2 negated-assertion
15	semantics, and why did Item 4 report an unavailable SysIDE license when a license exists?
16	
17	## Summary
18	
19	- R-1 is already determined by the owner-ratified numerical-profile contract: every ordering root
20	  is a numerical claim, and an ordering whose meaning cannot pass through the retained IEEE-double
21	  runtime is malformed and blocks generation. Boolean, String, and enumeration ordering therefore
22	  BLOCK; defining host-language ordering would reverse the selected scope.
23	- R-2 was presented as a false choice. Negation is already in the owner concept's first scope. The
24	  established architecture preserves the positive predicate body and usage polarity separately,
25	  derives expected truth from polarity, and applies polarity once when producing verdict and margin.
26	  The consistent repair is to make polarity explicit in `UsageDecision`, not fold it into IR and
27	  not block negated assertions.
28	- The recent license skips were caused by test invocation. `uv run` and the test configuration do
29	  not automatically load `.env`. Explicitly loading the new repo-local `.env` makes SysIDE import
30	  and all licensed Item 4 tests pass.
31	
32	## Decision Provenance
33	
34	### R-1: non-numeric ordering
35	
36	The owner-stated purpose is numerical validity evaluation. Non-numerical statements remain visible
37	but are outside execution, while malformed or unprovable numerical claims error
38	(`.project/active/numerical-constraint-profile/spec.md:19-31,65-73`). The owner also ratified the
39	IEEE-double runtime and the structural classifier: an ordering/arithmetic root is a numerical claim;
40	if it is not fully admitted, it BLOCKs (`spec.md:78-105`; `spec-review.md:155-174`;
41	`design.md:133-147`).
42	
43	The exact Boolean/String/enum ordering rows were not separately owner-originated. Their BLOCK result
44	is the direct application of that ratified rule. Admitting them would require a new typed runtime,
45	explicit Boolean and enum ordering definitions, typed schemas, compiler support, snapshot/evidence
46	changes, and a deliberate scope amendment. Python comparison behavior is not modeled semantics.
47	
48	### R-2: assertion negation
49	
50	The original owner concept includes negation in first scope and requires assertion polarity to
51	survive live extraction, snapshots, and execution unchanged
52	(`.project/concepts/constraint-execution-and-design-space-studies.md:81-87,141-147,231-237`). It
53	also states the separate-polarity model directly: assertion membership owns expected truth; normal
54	expects true and negated expects false (`constraint-execution-and-design-space-studies.md:295-303`).
55	The completed profile and owner-ratified numerical profile both include negated assertion polarity
56	(`../agentic-mbse/.project/completed/20260713_executable-profile/spec.md:139-146`;
57	`.project/active/numerical-constraint-profile/spec.md:35-39,90-93`).
58	
59	The current dataflow implements that split:
60	
61	1. Extraction selects the source predicate body and independently captures `is_negated`
62	   (`../agentic-mbse/src/agentic_mbse/sysml/constraint_extraction.py:666-693`).
63	2. The profile selects and walks the positive body, but currently omits polarity from its decision
64	   (`../agentic-mbse/src/agentic_mbse/sysml/executable_profile.py:717-783`). This omission is R-2.
65	3. Lowering verifies the same source IR, guards polarity, stores positive `predicate_ir`, and derives
66	   `expected_value = not is_negated` (`src/sysml_codegen/analysis/constraint_lowering.py:970-987,
67	   1083-1104`).
68	4. Models enforce that expected value derives from polarity
69	   (`src/sysml_codegen/resolution/models.py:387-438,454-482`).
70	5. The compiler returns the raw predicate value, compares it to false for a negated assertion, and
71	   flips only the simple-margin sign (`src/sysml_codegen/generation/predicate_compiler.py:232-302`).
72	   Execution pins a negated assertion as satisfied with raw `actual_value is False` and positive
73	   sign-flipped margin (`tests/execution/test_constraint_execution.py:509-544`).
74	
75	Folding negation into IR would break the same-source-IR invariant and change `actual_value` from the
76	raw modeled predicate to its assertion-level negation. Blocking negation would reverse the original
77	scope. The profile should instead consume/carry known polarity and derived expected truth, and
78	codegen should verify and consume that decision-carried value rather than independently re-reading
79	unclassified usage metadata. Polarity remains applied once at verdict/margin derivation.
80	
81	## License Findings
82	
83	There was a real expired license earlier in 2026, followed by a renewed key used by `fusion-tea`.
84	The recent Item 4 skip had a different cause: plain `uv run pytest ...` did not load the new
85	sysml-codegen `.env`, and `tests/conftest.py` has no automatic dotenv loader.
86	
87	Secret-safe successful commands used an explicit environment file or exported `.env` without
88	printing its value. Results on 2026-07-19:
89	
90	- SysIDE import: passed.
91	- Item 4 relocation file: 3/3 passed, including live A/live B/replay A.
92	- Item 4 focused suite: 407/407 passed normally and 407/407 under optimized Python.
93	- Full licensed repository suite, independently run during this investigation: 2,950 passed,
94	  26 skipped, 10 deselected.
95	
96	Preferred command pattern:
97	
98	```bash
99	UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/sysml-codegen-license-uv-cache \
100	  uv run --env-file .env pytest ...
101	```
102	
103	The repo-local `.env` is gitignored but currently mode `0664`; mode `0600` is preferable for a
104	secret file.
105	
106	## Recommendations
107	
108	1. Record R-1 as BLOCK for Boolean/String/enum ordering under the existing malformed-numerical
109	   diagnostic family. This applies the existing contract; it is not a new semantics choice.
110	2. Amend the Item 1 spec to replace the R-2 binary with the established third option: preserve
111	   source predicate IR, carry polarity explicitly in the profile decision, and apply it once
112	   downstream.
113	3. Add positive/negated x inline/definition-typed live and codec tests, plus a codegen invariant
114	   proving decision polarity, catalog polarity, expected truth, verdict, and margin agree.
115	4. Use `uv run --env-file .env` for licensed codegen gates and correct Item 4 audit/tracking from
116	   license-free certification to full certification.
117	
118	## Open Questions
119	
120	- Exact R-1 diagnostic code and repair wording are design details.
121	- The profile decision may carry only polarity or both polarity and derived expected truth. The
122	  design must keep one authoritative application path and reject missing/contradictory values.
123	- Whether to reduce `.env` permissions to `0600` is an operational action for the owner.
124

All paths under `/home/reid/1cfe/fusion-tea/exploration/ife_e2e/` (the PRIMARY checkout). teax runtime source referenced from `/home/reid/1cfe/teax/packages/teax-simkit/`.

## 1. The acceptance result (`study/findings.md`)

**Headline:** 100% agreement between the retiring hand rule and the now-executing generated constraint, modulo 7 flagged boundary rows. Confirmed against the artifact: `study/acceptance_table.csv` has 2301 data rows, 2294 exact matches, 7 boundary rows.

**What was replayed** (`findings.md:7-15`): the retiring hand rule at `sweep_ife.py:82` (`eta * gain > 10`, strict `>`) and the generated `'Viability Threshold'` constraint assertion (`eta * gain >= threshold`, `>=`) were run together over the full 2301-point `(eta, gain)` grid — `ETA_GRID` (39 pts) × `G_GRID` (59 pts), matching `sweep_ife.py`'s grid exactly.

**The `>` vs `>=` divergence (7 rows):** the 7 rows sit exactly on `eta*gain == 10.0`. I pulled them from the CSV — every one has `old_viable=False, new_verdict=satisfied, new_viable=True, at_boundary=True, match=True`:

```
eta,   gain,  eta_g, old_viable, new_verdict, new_viable, at_boundary, match
0.04,  250.0, 10.0,  False,      satisfied,   True,       True,        True
0.05,  200.0, 10.0,  False,      satisfied,   True,       True,        True
0.08,  125.0, 10.0,  False,      satisfied,   True,       True,        True
0.10,  100.0, 10.0,  False,      satisfied,   True,       True,        True
0.199..,50.0, 10.0,  False,      satisfied,   True,       True,        True
0.25,  40.0,  10.0,  False,      satisfied,   True,       True,        True
0.40,  25.0,  10.0,  False,      satisfied,   True,       True,        True
```

The strict `>` hand rule rejects the exact boundary; the model's `>=` accepts it. This is documented as a known boundary hazard (`.project/reference/fusion-tea-ife-sweep/FACTS.md`), flagged not reconciled away. The `at_boundary` flag makes `match=True` despite the raw `old_viable != new_viable` (see `run_viability_study.py:158-162`).

**Hand-rule retirement (`sweep_ife.py:82`):** `findings.md:17-22` — the hot grid loop now calls the generated predicate function `ife_tea.modules.constraints.predicates.constraint_pred_ife_plant__ife_power_plant__viability` directly, the same mechanical-import pattern the file already used for LCOE/recirculating-fraction. Confirmed in `sweep_ife.py:45-47` (import) and `:93-96` (call → `verdict.status == "satisfied"`). The LCOE-threshold overlay at `sweep_ife.py:98` (`attractive = viable and power_positive and lcoe <= 100`) is deliberately left hand-coded — it is policy, not a modeled constraint.

**"Regeneration changed nothing about numerics" (`findings.md:29-39`):** `generated/` was regenerated live from `models/` against sysml-codegen's `constraint-exec-epic` branch — 8 modules now (was 6 pre-epic), the two new ones being `HifPlantViabilityConstraintModule` and `ConstraintReportAggregatorModule`. Anchors A/B/C in `run_anchors.py` re-verified byte-exact against pre-existing numbers: LCOE $252.29996307 / $68.69020165 / $270.12117794, Meier COE 4.735 c/kWh.
